minutes.headline: Sewer Commission accepted the 7-Eleven Mass Ave condo plans and assessed a privilege fee for 17 Highland Street.
minutes.summary: New chair John Reynolds ran his first meeting. The commission accepted the 7-Eleven condo project plans, assessed a connection privilege fee for 17 Highland Street, approved the May 31 minutes, and approved a changed bond amount on the CTE contract. Also discussed were the Upland/Eastern Ab White Maple Street extension survey, the Alfonso's building question, a pump station tour, and meeting format.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission voted to accept the plan review for the 7-Eleven Mass Ave condo project, a large project application.
The commission approved a privilege fee assessment for 17 Highland Street; the commitment goes to the assessors, with a 30-day letter to follow.
The commission approved the CTE contract with a changed bond amount, which rose slightly.
The June 28 meeting will stay on Zoom, and the July 12 format is to be discussed later.
Sewer budget status and capital requests, including pump and control panel items, were sent to the next agenda, with the DPW director invited.

why_it_matters: A connection off an earlier sewer extension is charged the standard privilege fee rather than the betterment amount, which sets what a property owner in that position pays.
The Maple Street extension survey and the pump and control panel requests feed the sewer budget, and the commission will return to both.
watch_next: The June 28 meeting on Zoom, where the commission is to take up the sewer budget status and fiscal 2023 spending with the DPW director invited.
A second mailing to residents on the Maple Street extension.
